scope: The Stone generator of K1356's genuine compact-circle restriction on the complete unitary principal-series Hilbert space and its K-finite core; not a proof that the source action selects this domain or that the interacting nonlinear quotient closes on it.

stone_generator.circle_action: U(alpha)=pi([exp(alpha e1e2),1]) is a strongly continuous unitary representation of R/(2 pi Z)
stone_generator.generator: U(alpha)=exp(i alpha Q) with Q self-adjoint by Stone's theorem
stone_generator.spectral_decomposition: H_ps is the Hilbert direct sum of integer charge spaces H_q
stone_generator.operator_domain: D(Q)={v=sum_q v_q: sum_q q^2 ||v_q||^2 is finite}
stone_generator.core: the algebraic K-finite subspace H_Kfin is dense, C-invariant, a finite charge sum on each vector, and a core for Q
stone_generator.sector_boundary: each H_q is C-invariant, while a nonzero fixed H_q is not invariant under full G by K1352

unboundedness_witness.family: for every n>=1, the M-spherical harmonic K-type Sym^(2n)_0(R^7_C) tensor 1 occurs in L2(K/M)
unboundedness_witness.M_fixed_witness: the harmonic projection of x1^(2n) is nonzero and M-fixed because every split-sign element changes x1 only by a sign
unboundedness_witness.extreme_charges: the selected spin-circle has charges plus_or_minus 4n on the highest and lowest two-plane monomials
unboundedness_witness.conclusion: the integer spectrum of Q is unbounded in both signs
unboundedness_witness.domain_is_proper: choosing normalized vectors at charges q_n=4n with coefficients 1/n gives a Hilbert vector because sum 1/n^2 converges but not a D(Q) vector because sum q_n^2/n^2 diverges

claim_ceiling: The selected compact circle has an honest self-adjoint integer charge generator on the completed principal series, with a dense invariant K-finite core and exact graph domain. Its spectrum is unbounded in both signs, so replacing K1346's scalar charge by Q creates a real common-domain obligation rather than a bounded relabeling.
